extracted.subtask_description: An excerpt from a speculative novel describing a Europe-wide political crisis and the papal response, including an allocution that prescribes an Order and forbids certain secular movements. The text contains narrative plus explicit prescriptive clauses issued by the Pope (rules, prohibitions, and institutional arrangements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of Felsenburgh's Presidency of Europe
rubrics_metrics.description: Felsenburgh is offered and accepts a new supranational office described as 'President of Europe' with specified powers and constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated terms (verbatim/close paraphrase): he should receive 'a House of Government in every capital of Europe'; his veto of any measure 'should be final for three years'; any measure he chose to introduce 'three times in three consecutive years should become law'; his title to be 'President of Europe'; from his side 'practically nothing was asked, except that he should refuse any other official position offered him that did not receive the sanction of all the Powers.' Context notes: the offer concentrates substantial legislative and veto power in one individual and is presented as creating the danger of 'an united Europe increased tenfold' and the combination of Socialism with individual brilliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papal condemnation of secular-unity movements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pope formally condemns and anathematises opinions and organisations that seek unity on any foundation other than a divine one, forbidding Catholics from joining or supporting such bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated guidance (verbatim/close paraphrase): 'we once more condemn and anathematise the opinions of those who teach and believe the contrary of this; and we renew once more all the condemnations ... against all those societies, organisations and communities that have been formed for the furtherance of an unity on another than a divine foundation; and We remind Our children throughout the world that it is forbidden to them to enter or to aid or to approve in any manner whatsoever any of those bodies named in such condemnations.' The allocution frames this as continuity with past condemnations (e.g., references to Freemasonry) and as a necessary defence because worldly 'peace and unity' are seen as deficient without peace with God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutional conditions of the Order of Christ Crucified
rubrics_metrics.description: The Pope institutes an Order (the Order of Christ Crucified) with explicit conditions, purposes and structural rules for admission, governance, and future promotion within Church hierarchy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Stated conditions and provisions (verbatim/close paraphrase):
- 'None shall be capable of entering the Order except such as shall be above the age of seventeen years.'
- 'No badge, habit, nor insignia shall be attached to it.'
- 'The Three Evangelical Counsels shall be the foundation of the Rule, to which we add a fourth intention, namely, that of a desire to receive the crown of martyrdom and a purpose of embracing it.'
- 'The bishop of every diocese, if he himself shall enter the Order, shall be the superior within the limits of his own jurisdiction, and alone shall be exempt from the literal observance of the Vow of Poverty so long as he retains his see.'
- 'Such bishops as do not feel the vocation to the Order shall retain their sees under the usual conditions, but shall have no Religious claim on the members of the Order.'
- 'We announce Our intention of Ourself entering the Order as its supreme prelate, and of making Our profession within the course of a few days.'
- 'In Our Own pontificate none shall be elevated to the Sacred College save those who have made their profession in the Order.'
- The Basilica of St. Peter and St. Paul will be dedicated as the central church of the Order and 'We shall raise to the altars without any delay those happy souls who shall lay down their lives in the pursuance of their vocation.'
- 'As regards the novitiate, its conditions and requirements, we shall shortly issue the necessary directions.'
Context/explanatory guidance: the allocution frames the Order as a divine response to a new worldly power; although 'obedient service will be required,' the 'primary intention' is an offering to God rather than human institutional ends. Some matters are reserved as 'secret' to be treated later, and practical novitiate rules are promised subsequently.
